check.population: every boundary, wrapper and composite structure that sits between a caller and the objects it uses
check.freshness: a verdict stands until the wrapped interface or its callers change
check.refusal: the boundary import rule or the conformance test fails a caller that reaches past the structure
check.observation: imports and call sites that cross the structure, read from source
check.evidence: none: the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it
check.authority: the structure's interface, which every caller goes through

distinctFrom.reason: An adapter fits one incompatible interface to the one expected, while an anti-corruption layer translates a whole external model into the local domain's terms.

records.name: Adapter Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern that wraps a component with an incompatible interface so it implements the interface its callers expect.

records.name: Facade Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern that gives a subsystem one simple entry point, so callers do not depend on its parts.

records.name: Proxy Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern that places a stand-in with the same interface in front of an object, to control, defer or cache access to it.

records.name: Bridge Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern that separates two independent axes of variation into two hierarchies joined by composition.

records.name: Decorator Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern that adds behavior to an object by wrapping it in another object with the same interface.

records.name: Composite Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern that gives leaves and groups one interface, so a tree is traversed without checking which kind each node is.

records.name: Flyweight Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern that shares one copy of immutable intrinsic state among many objects, each keeping only its own extrinsic state.
detected_by: repeated equal intrinsic state across objects
